reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 14.1 keeps Customer ownership of Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP with only a limited processing right to Vendor; Section 14.2 vests Deliverables in Customer with an express Vendor assignment, personnel assignments and further assurance; Section 14.3 limits Vendor retention to Vendor Technology (defined to exclude Customer Data and pre-existing Customer IP) and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence including modification and derivative works; Section 14.4 blocks joint ownership absent a signed instrument setting exploitation rights.

No assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor and no vendor-owned-deliverable-without-licence pattern appears, consistent with the deterministic check; the rule's walk-away triggers are absent.
Correctly presented with no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding retained as internal evidence.

Minor rationale inaccuracy worth noting internally (not a basis to fail): the Customer Data definition at 1.9/1.3 does contain a narrow carve-out for anonymized operational telemetry, so the statement that 'no aggregated/de-identified data carve-out exists' is overstated; the carve-out is limited to data that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer or an individual and does not defeat the preferred position. Section 14.1's processing right to 'improve the Services' is likewise a use right, not an ownership transfer.
